title: Layered preflight overlay and migration-hooks: tenant mapping & portable probes
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add composable preflight overlay and migration hook templates for Private Helm installs; introduces tenant-aware node/taint overlays, a portable probe helper for air-gapped installers, and a dry-run migration hook mode. Backwards compatible; opt-in via values.preflight.enableOverlay.
description:
Motivation: Private deployments require flexible, composable preflight checks and safer migration/upgrade hooks that work across VPC and air-gapped on-prem installs. Current init hooks are monolithic for tenant bootstrap and make it hard to add environment-specific probes (e.g. restricted networks) without forking charts. This PR introduces a layered overlay approach to preflight and migration hook templates that (1) lets ops compose probes per-deployment, (2) surfaces a portable probe helper for air-gapped environments, and (3) adds a dry-run migration mode and safer rollback fence to reduce upgrade blast radius.

Summary of changes: added a new values overlay section (values.preflight.overlays) that composes a sequence of overlay fragments. Each fragment can inject templated initJobs, probeConfig, nodeAffinity/taints, and mount overlays. Introduced chart helpers/_probe-helpers.tpl and _overlay-merge.tpl to keep templates DRY; helper supports kube-probe wrapper for environments without external curl/hostnames. Added migration-hooks/migrate-dryrun Job template and a migration-fence-configmap that records migration phases for rollback safety. New values schema (values.schema.json) includes schema for overlays, minimumProbeConfig, and a new preflight.enabled flag.

Backward compatibility and safety: Default behavior is unchanged unless values.preflight.enableOverlay is set. Migration dry-run is opt-in via values.migration.dryRun=true. Hook templates include weightedHook annotations (hook-weight) and a preflight.gateConfig to allow orchestrators to gate upgrades (e.g. via private-installer controller). We added a feature toggle values.preflight.usePortableProbes to switch to the portable probe image for air-gapped installs.

Testing and rollout: unit/template tests added under templates/tests/preflight-overlay-test.yaml and a set of k8s manifest samples in examples/preflight-overlays/ that demonstrate tenant-mapping overlay (multi-tenant nodeAffinity), bare-metal probe (hostpath) and an airgapped scenario. CI runs lint, template unit-tests and smoke integration against KinD. We manually exercised a staged rollout in our staging cluster (redwood-staging) using canary releases and verified that the migration-dryrun writes the expected fence keys and does not mutate tenant data.

Docs and next steps: updated docs/helm/private/preflight.md with examples and recommended overlays for VPC vs on-prem. Filed a followup to add a private-installer controller hook to read gateConfig and coordinate tenant waves (ENG-15948). Also opened a small PR in redwood-private-installer to consume values.preflight.overlays by name.

Related: ENG-15932 (preflight overhaul), ENG-15948 (installer orchestration), SUP-983 (customer onprem upgrade fallout), and a docs task PM-4321.

review_comments: Luca Moretti: Can we keep the default probe image unchanged for hosted deployments? I don't want change to leak into hosted path. -> Author: yes, the portable probe image is opt-in (preflight.usePortableProbes=false by default).

Nina Patel: The overlay merge logic looks complex; can we add more unit tests for conflicting keys? -> Author: added conflict-resolution tests and documented that later fragments override earlier ones, plus a validation precheck in values.schema.json.

Jorge Alvarez: Will migration-fence affect rollback time? We need to ensure small windows. -> Author: fence is a small ConfigMap write; documented expected latency and added retries/backoff to the hook template.
